name: WeftMark
tagline: Confidence should have a chain of reasons.
description: Engineering provenance for human–agent teams: connect the purpose of a change, its permitted scope, exact Git lineage, evidence, review and handoff. Make a decision inspectable after the worker and the conversation have gone.
status: Prototype · local evidence and review workflows implemented; not a production-certified control plane
motifCaption: The loom: separate threads, a record another person can examine.

sv.title: WeftMark
sv.description: Förtroende behöver en kedja av skäl. WeftMark håller samman ändringens syfte, tillåten omfattning, Git-historik, underlag, granskning och överlämning när människor och AI-agenter arbetar tillsammans.

sections.title: Förtroende som går att undersöka
paragraphs: WeftMark är en prototyp för teknisk proveniens, underlag och granskning. Genomförd, verifierad, granskad och publicerad är olika tillstånd. Ett godkänt test måste knytas till den version det faktiskt kontrollerade.

De engelska fördjupningarna visar ett körbart exempel, sambanden med Rebekah och Nostoi samt hur dokumentation och loggar kan bidra till ett arbete med EU:s AI-förordning. Det innebär inte att verktyget i sig intygar regelefterlevnad.

sections.title: Väv, verkstad och vittne
paragraphs: WeftMark organiserar tekniska ändringar och granskningsbeslut. Sylvae sparar körningsunderlag. Nostoi granskar kompatibla loggkedjor och stödjer externa kontrollpunkter. Rebekah paketerar och avgränsar körmiljön; Ephor är ett separat, frivilligt lager för styrning.
Exempelutforskaren och fördjupningarna publiceras tills vidare på engelska. De blandar inte ihop lokal verifiering, oberoende granskning och ett beslut om driftsättning.

featuredPublication.label: The evidence problem / Brief 01
featuredPublication.imageAlt: A Change Set connects intent, scope and Git revision with evidence, review and handoff; ledger integrity is a separate Nostoi check.

highlights.label: 01 / Authority
highlights.title: Scope is more than a list of files
highlights.text: A worker can obey a file boundary and still change a protocol. Record the semantic contract and the authority for changing it, alongside the paths.

highlights.label: 02 / Evidence
highlights.title: A passing test has an address
highlights.text: Bind an evidence result to the clean commit it inspected. If the code moves, the old pass remains historical evidence—not current assurance.

highlights.label: 03 / Judgment
highlights.title: A review is a recorded decision
highlights.text: Keep who evaluated which evidence, under which policy, and what remains unresolved. A signature, a page view and a release are different observations.

sections.title: The scarce resource is justified confidence.
paragraphs: When several people and AI workers can produce changes quickly, the bottleneck shifts from writing to explaining. Why was this change allowed? What actually changed? Which checks cover this revision? Who accepted the remaining uncertainty, and what did they authorise next?

WeftMark makes those questions durable through a Change Set. It binds a goal, file and semantic scopes, Git base and head, evidence, review and handoff. It is a vendor-neutral local ledger around the work, rather than another model, coding agent or issue tracker.

The runtime and read-only reviewer surfaces are implemented as prototype software. The repository's assurance record distinguishes implemented, verified, reviewed and releasable capabilities. A deployed explanatory website does not upgrade that runtime into a production-certified platform.

sections.title: Permission before production of evidence.
paragraphs: File scopes say where a worker may edit. Semantic scopes say which meaning is in play: an API contract, evidence policy, identity boundary or retention rule. Two changes to different files may conflict because both alter the same promise to a caller.

During the current migration, Frog remains the operational scheduler and lock coordinator. Native WeftMark claims do not override a Frog lock, and imported assignments remain observations until explicitly promoted. Authority is kept with its owner instead of inferred from whichever screen looks most recent.

sections.title: A receipt is useful only if its binding survives.
paragraphs: Evidence needs a kind, result, producer, command or observation source, and a binding to the work it inspected. Passed, failed, unavailable and stale are not four colours for the same state. An unavailable check did not run; a stale pass may still describe an older revision correctly.

The local evidence runner invokes an argument vector, not a shell string, and records its result. It is not a sandbox for hostile commands. Production operation still needs resource limits, secret handling, trusted runners and access controls supplied by the environment.

The demonstration below lets you explore those distinctions without connecting to a real ledger or approving anything. The linked CLI walkthrough exercises the actual prototype: ready at one head, stale after a new commit, and ready again after fresh evidence.

sections.title: A workshop with distinct authorities.
paragraphs: Rebekah packages a self-hosted OCI runtime with supervised services, state separation and an authenticated gateway. OpenCode supplies agent sessions; Ollama supplies local inference; Sylvae executes portable skills and preserves run evidence. WeftMark connects that work to engineering scope, Git lineage and review.

Nostoi asks whether compatible ledger records remain internally consistent and supports external checkpoints and signed attestations. WeftMark asks what a change means and whether its required evidence and review are current. A valid ledger does not establish that the test was sufficient, the reviewer independent, or the release authorised.

Ephor is the opt-in governance authority. Rebekah's governed connector and WeftMark's native review are separate paths: a native readiness decision must not be relabelled as an Ephor approval. Git and the forge remain the source of commit, CI, publication and merge facts.

sections.title: Separate an assertion from an observation.
paragraphs: A configured model name is not necessarily the model served. A harness name is not the person who authorised an action. A submitted actor label is not authenticated identity. Useful provenance states who supplied each claim, what was independently observed, and which facts are still unknown.

For a professional evidence package, preserve the revision, dependency and environment identity, model/provider observations where available, tool and dataset references, the capture interval, and the reviewer policy. Retain only information the purpose requires; raw prompts, personal data and credentials should not become permanent public ledger entries.

WeftMark provides a structure for engineering evidence and producer correlation, not an automatic attestation of every upstream provider statement. A Sylvae run ID, a forge observation and a Nostoi verification report contribute different evidence and should retain their own boundaries.

sections.title: Turn obligations into evidence questions.
paragraphs: The EU AI Act is role- and risk-dependent. A software team using an AI assistant is not automatically the provider of a high-risk AI system. First determine intended purpose, classification, operator role and the applicable version and timetable of the law.

For relevant high-risk systems, Articles 11 and 12 address technical documentation and automatic event recording; Articles 14 and 26 address meaningful human oversight; Article 15 addresses accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity. Change Sets and review records can support the engineering story, but they do not replace system-level logging, data governance, risk management or conformity assessment.

The current Commission sources incorporate the July 2026 AI Omnibus changes: Annex III high-risk requirements apply from 2 December 2027 and the relevant Annex I product pathway from 2 August 2028. Other obligations have earlier application dates. Our detailed mapping is dated, links its sources and does not present WeftMark as an AI Act certification tool.

links.label: The dated AI Act evidence mapping

sections.title: Build for scrutiny, not only for today's throughput.
paragraphs: Professional agent systems need bounded authority, reproducible evaluation, failure reporting, credential isolation, an intervention path and a record another team can reconstruct. As capabilities grow, capture the effects of actions and the conditions of evaluation rather than substituting an agent's confident narrative for evidence.

Model changes, retrieval sources, tool permissions and deployment environments can change without a source-code diff. Review policy therefore needs to consider those changes explicitly, including evaluation drift, incident response and rollback. An exact Git head is a valuable anchor, but not a complete description of a deployed AI system.

The goal is a legible chain of reasons: enough evidence to challenge a claim, enough separation of authority to refuse a shortcut, and a handoff that survives a session. That supports trust without pretending to eliminate uncertainty or solve AI alignment by record-keeping alone.

workflow.title: Declare purpose and authority
workflow.text: State the outcome, allowed files and semantic contracts. Inspect Frog assignment and locks during the transition; acquire the native claim from the actual worktree.

workflow.title: Observe the exact revision
workflow.text: Record the base, branch, head and dirty paths. Do not reuse an old head's passing results as assurance for a new one.

workflow.title: Collect typed evidence
workflow.text: Capture test, CI, security, deployment or documentation evidence with its producer and binding. Record unavailable or stale checks honestly.

workflow.title: Review and hand over deliberately
workflow.text: Record the decision, unresolved issues, next actor and action. Obtain publication and merge facts from Git and the forge, not from a status label.

quickstart.title: A local experiment in evidence freshness
quickstart.summary: Install the prototype from source, then use a disposable Git repository with a valid HEAD. The example verifies only a small fixture—not an AI system or a production release.
quickstart.note: Use your own local Git identity for the fixture commits. The example-author review is an author review, not an independent approval. Full commands and the stale-head experiment are in the demonstration brief.

commands.label: Install from source
commands.code:
git clone https://github.com/tabenius/WeftMark.git
cd WeftMark
python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
pip install .

commands.label: Create a harmless, committed fixture
commands.code:
mkdir weftmark-lab
cd weftmark-lab
git init
printf 'result = "reviewable"\n' > example.txt
git add example.txt
git commit -m "Start an evidence experiment"

commands.label: Bind one check to its clean head
commands.code:
weftmark changeset create demo \
  --goal "Demonstrate exact-head evidence" --scope 'file:**'
weftmark evidence run demo --kind test --command \
  python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; assert Path("example.txt").exists()'
weftmark review create demo --author example-author --require test

demonstration.label: The evidence desk / Illustrated cases
demonstration.title: The same green result can mean different things.
demonstration.description: Select a case to inspect the relationship between evidence, revision and review. H1 and H2 are symbolic revision labels, not fabricated commit receipts.
demonstration.disclaimer: Presentation-only illustrations. No command runs, no live ledger is inspected, and no review or publication is authorised by this explorer.

cases.title: Current evidence, bounded review
cases.description: The evidence result and current clean head refer to the same revision.
cases.conclusion: Illustration: the stated evidence requirement can be satisfied. This does not establish production release, legal conformity or independent review.

cases.title: A new commit makes the old pass stale
cases.description: The branch advances while the retained test receipt still names the earlier head.
cases.conclusion: Illustration: rerun the relevant check and evaluate the new receipt. The old test remains a historical pass, not a current one.

cases.title: Unavailable is not passed, or failed
cases.description: A required assessment could not be performed.
cases.conclusion: Illustration: record the missing evidence and the next action. Do not manufacture a pass or describe the underlying system as failing a test that never ran.

cases.title: An intact ledger is a different finding
cases.description: A chain check succeeds, but the review has not established the adequacy of the underlying work.
cases.conclusion: Illustration: Nostoi continuity evidence complements WeftMark's review; it cannot replace an authorised judgment about sufficient tests or acceptable risk.

pages.title: A chain of reasons for an engineering decision
pages.description: Purpose, bounded work, exact-head evidence, review and handoff—each with its own authority and limits.

sections.title: The permission belongs before the edit.
paragraphs: Read the repository instructions and intended task. Identify file and semantic scope, dependencies and refusal criteria before acquiring the native claim. During migration, Frog locks remain a separate operational requirement.

A scope declaration is not the same as enforcement against every possible side effect. The worker's runtime must still constrain filesystem, process and network authority. WeftMark records the engineering boundary; Rebekah and other execution environments enforce their own controls.

sections.title: Preserve the reference, not just the result.
paragraphs: Bind each check to the clean head and capture its command, producer and outcome. A changed revision needs a new evaluation of what remains applicable. Missing infrastructure, failed assertions and stale receipts answer different questions.

Evidence volume is not evidence quality. A receipt from a trivial fixture check is useful to demonstrate a mechanism; it is not a safety assessment. Required evidence policy must match the actual change and consequence.

sections.title: Name the judgment and its limits.
paragraphs: Review records should explain which evidence was considered and which uncertainty remains. A supplied reviewer identifier needs its own identity/authorization context; an author review must not be presented as independent oversight.
A decision about local readiness is not evidence that a forge merged the change or that a production service deployed it. Those facts come from Git, the forge and deployment observations.

sections.title: Leave enough structure to continue.
paragraphs: A handoff names the exact head, current evidence, open findings, next action and receiver. That is a compact working record another person can use without importing an entire conversation.

Provenance survives when each subsystem keeps its own authority: session identity, engineering lineage, runtime observations and external signatures should be linked, not collapsed into one reassuring label.

pages.title: Watch a passing receipt become stale
pages.description: A reproducible local CLI experiment, followed by fresh evidence and a compatible Nostoi ledger check.

sections.title: A fixture, not a production assessment.
paragraphs: Install WeftMark from source in a virtual environment, then create a separate Git repository with at least one committed file. Use the homepage quickstart to create the demo Change Set and its first test receipt.

The test checks only that example.txt exists. That narrow assertion is intentional: the experiment demonstrates revision binding and stale evidence, not the correctness or safety of a deployed AI system. The example-author review is not independent approval.

sections.title: Advance the head without repeating the check.
paragraphs: After the initial review reports ready, commit a change to the fixture and refresh the Change Set. The old passing receipt still names the earlier commit. In the checked local prototype, the following review reports stale and exits with status 5.
sections.code:
printf '# A new revision\n' >> example.txt
git add example.txt
git commit -m "Advance the example revision"
weftmark changeset refresh demo
weftmark review create demo --author example-author --require test
printf 'review exit=%s\n' "$?"

sections.title: Produce evidence for the new revision.
paragraphs: Run the same small check again at the clean new head and create another policy review. The checked experiment returns ready again. The history keeps both receipts and explains why the first stopped supporting current readiness.
sections.code:
weftmark evidence run demo --kind test --command \
  python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; assert Path("example.txt").exists()'
weftmark review create demo --author example-author --require test

sections.title: Ask Nostoi a different question.
paragraphs: In an ordinary standalone Git fixture, WeftMark keeps ledger.jsonl under the common Git directory's weftmark folder. Nostoi can verify its compatible ledger format. Linked worktrees share a common Git directory, so resolve it rather than assuming .git is a directory.

A successful integrity check says the retained record is internally consistent. It does not approve the example review, authenticate the author label, or prove that all significant actions were captured.
sections.code:
# With the Nostoi CLI installed:
nostoi verify "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/weftmark/ledger.jsonl"

pages.title: EU AI Act: an evidence mapping, not a certificate
pages.description: A dated connection between engineering records and applicable logging, documentation, oversight and lifecycle obligations.

sections.title: Start with the role, system and intended purpose.
paragraphs: Reviewed 5 October 2026 using the Commission's current overview and AI Act Service Desk text, which identifies the consolidated version as at 27 July 2026. Provider, deployer and general-purpose-model duties differ; intended purpose and the classification rules matter. An engineering ledger does not classify a system or decide whether an exemption applies.

The Commission reports the July 2026 AI Omnibus entering into force on 27 July 2026, with Annex III high-risk requirements applying from 2 December 2027 and the relevant Annex I product pathway from 2 August 2028. Transparency rules and general-purpose-model rules have earlier timelines. Check the current legal text and transitional provisions for the actual system.

sections.title: Documentation describes the system; changes explain its evolution.
paragraphs: Articles 11 and 17 concern technical documentation and the provider's quality-management system, with Annex IV describing documentation content. Change Sets can help organise development changes, verification references and decisions, but they do not supply a complete technical file or organisational quality system.

Risk management, data governance, evaluation methods and post-market monitoring have separate obligations under Articles 9, 10 and 72. A traceable fix is useful evidence within those processes; it does not substitute for their system-level content.

sections.title: Engineering receipts are not the whole operational log.
paragraphs: Article 12 requires relevant high-risk systems to technically allow automatic event recording over their lifetime, supporting traceability, monitoring and identification of risks or substantial modifications. An engineering ledger records the software-workflow story; the deployed AI system still needs instrumentation for its own relevant events.

Articles 19 and 26(6) address provider and deployer retention of automatically generated logs under their control, for an appropriate period of at least six months unless applicable Union or national law provides otherwise, notably data-protection law. This is not a universal requirement to store all prompts or all personal data for six months. Purpose, control and applicable law remain part of the decision.

sections.title: Human oversight needs capacity to act.
paragraphs: Article 14 concerns high-risk system design for human oversight; Article 26(2) requires deployers to assign it to people with competence, training, authority and support. A review button alone is not meaningful oversight. The person needs understandable evidence, time, an intervention path and authority to refuse or suspend use.

WeftMark can preserve an engineering review and its rationale. Production identity, permission checks and independent review must still be implemented in their own authorities. Article 15's accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity requirements need relevant testing of the AI system, not merely a passing build or valid ledger hash.

sections.title: Preserve the difference between support and conformity.
paragraphs: A procurement or investigation can ask for the revision, evaluation methods, evidence capture interval, operating conditions, review identity and authority, relevant incident history and retention policy. WeftMark, Nostoi and Rebekah can contribute different parts of that technical record.

The applicable conformity-assessment route, declaration, registration duties, fundamental-rights impact assessment where required and any specific sector obligations remain separate questions. WeftMark is a prototype evidence tool, not a notified body, legal adviser or compliance certificate.

pages.title: Rebekah's workshop: purpose, execution, evidence and custody
pages.description: How WeftMark, Nostoi, Sylvae, OpenCode, Ollama and optional Ephor contribute distinct parts of a professional system.

sections.title: Rebekah supplies the operating boundary.
paragraphs: Rebekah builds an OCI runtime with Nix, supervising services with separate identities and state directories. Its gateway authenticates access and exposes allowlisted backend routes; internal service health and failures have their own lifecycle. It remains an executable bootstrap rather than a production-ready distribution.
The website is explanatory. It is not a public gateway to your local repository, agent server or evidence runner. Deploying this page does not expose the prototype's local control surfaces.

sections.title: Workers produce actions; run records supply context.
paragraphs: OpenCode hosts agent sessions and workspace interaction. Ollama provides local inference. Sylvae executes portable skill instructions across supported backends and retains run identities and evidence. Those are execution responsibilities, not engineering approval.

A WeftMark producer reference can correlate evidence with a Sylvae run. Correlation should preserve the original source and limits; it should not imply authenticated model identity or independent assessment merely because a run has an ID.

sections.title: Nostoi preserves a different answer.
paragraphs: WeftMark's compatible ledger can be inspected with Nostoi. Sequence verification, an externally retained checkpoint and a deliberately verified signature have different meanings. They can strengthen custody of the engineering record without turning that record's claims into proven facts.

Keep signing keys with their operator and external references outside the producer's authority. An intact chain with insufficient tests is still insufficient evidence; a signed stale head is still a statement about an older position.

sections.title: Policy is not inferred from a status card.
paragraphs: Ephor is opt-in governance. When a governed action is requested, Rebekah's connector has its own fail-closed behavior. Native WeftMark review remains native review, and runtime snapshots remain observations rather than permissions.

The boundaries make the architecture explainable: runtime isolation, task authority, execution evidence, ledger integrity, human review and governance policy can each be examined without guessing that one subsystem certified all the others.

pages.title: A dossier that survives its author
pages.description: The technical expectations behind trust: exact references, qualified observations, intervention and a usable handoff.

sections.title: Reference the work and the conditions.
paragraphs: A useful dossier links intent and authority to an exact revision, dependencies, environment, data/tool references and evaluation conditions. Provider-reported model identity and directly observed serving identity should remain distinguishable.
Where an observation is absent, say unknown. A producer-supplied label can be useful metadata without becoming a verified assertion about a person, model or time.

sections.title: Coverage and failure are part of provenance.
paragraphs: Record the capture interval, known omissions, failed or unavailable checks and conditions under which prior results become stale. A durable history is not necessarily a complete one, and a small passing test is not necessarily representative.

As agents gain broader tool access, evidence should cover refusal paths, changed authority, retrieval and model updates, execution limits and recovery. These are engineering expectations; each deployment needs its own risk-appropriate criteria.

sections.title: The reviewer needs more than a dashboard.
paragraphs: Connect review to a verified identity and delegated authority in the production system. Explain the criterion, provide a way to challenge or suspend the action, and retain the decision and remaining uncertainty.

Read-only phone and tablet projections make the record easier to inspect. A view is not an approval receipt, and convenience should not silently broaden the authority of the person holding the device.

sections.title: Structure is a form of care.
paragraphs: A compact handoff names the current head, evidence bindings, open findings and next action. It helps a colleague continue without reproducing an entire conversation or inheriting hidden assumptions.

WeftMark's value is that inspectable structure. The professional expectation is not certainty; it is an honest account of why a decision was taken, which facts support it, and what would make it necessary to reconsider.
